boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Syracuse University
boards.description: Verified food destinations with evening or late-night availability on or near Syracuse University.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: 137 Marshall St, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: Check the location’s ordering page or call ahead before leaving; its listed late hours make it a dessert-focused option near the university.
cards.short_summary: A Marshall Street cookie shop with the latest listed hours in this set.
cards.evidence_claim: The Syracuse location is listed at 137 Marshall Street, with hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 11 a.m.–1 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday; 11 a.m.–3 a.m. Thursday–Friday; noon–3 a.m. Saturday. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Over The Cuse Pizza & Wings
cards.subtitle: 399 S Crouse Ave, CODA Building
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online ordering page to confirm the day’s availability, then plan pickup at the Crouse Avenue CODA Building location.
cards.short_summary: Pizza, wings, and other carryout items on South Crouse Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The restaurant’s ordering page lists the 399 South Crouse Avenue location and hours until 1:30 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Over The Cuse Pizza & Wings — online ordering
cards.access_notes: Listed hours run to 1:30 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; Monday–Wednesday are listed to 11:30 p.m. Confirm before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Over the Cuse Deli and Grill
cards.title: Over the Cuse Deli and Grill
cards.subtitle: 712 E Fayette St, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: Use the contact page’s weekly schedule when timing a pickup; Thursday through Saturday have the latest listed closing times.
cards.short_summary: A deli-and-grill destination east of campus with weekend late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Over the Cuse Deli and Grill lists its Fayette Street address and hours until 2 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Over the Cuse Deli and Grill — Contact
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: midnight Monday–Wednesday and 2 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; closed Sunday. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Syracuse Halal Gyro
cards.subtitle: 477 Westcott St, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: This Westcott Street stop lists takeout and limited seating; check its current ordering status before heading over late.
cards.short_summary: A halal-food destination on Westcott Street with very late listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse Halal Gyro is listed at 477 Westcott Street, and the Westcott Community page lists its hours as 10 a.m.–3 a.m.
cards.source_title: Westcott Grocery & Syracuse Halal Gyro — Westcott Community
cards.access_notes: The Westcott Community listing gives Syracuse Halal Gyro hours as 10 a.m.–3 a.m. The restaurant’s site says takeout and limited seating; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Franco's Pizzeria & Deli
cards.subtitle: 901 E Genesee St, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: For a late delivery run, check the restaurant’s service area and minimum first; the site specifically includes Syracuse University.
cards.short_summary: An East Genesee pizzeria and deli that lists overnight delivery service.
cards.evidence_claim: Franco’s lists delivery to Syracuse University and surrounding areas until 3 a.m. daily; Friday and Saturday menu hours are listed until midnight.
cards.access_notes: The site lists delivery to the university and surrounding areas until 3 a.m. daily, with a $15 delivery minimum. Confirm before ordering.

cards.title: Tazza
cards.subtitle: 466 Westcott St, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: Plan around the published daily schedule and use the Westcott Street address for an evening food stop rather than assuming all services run late.
cards.short_summary: A Westcott Street restaurant listing midnight closing most nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Tazza lists hours until midnight Monday through Saturday and until 10 p.m. Sunday at 466 Westcott Street.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 11 a.m.–midnight Monday–Saturday and 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Sunday. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Funk 'n Waffles
cards.subtitle: 307–13 S Clinton St, Syracuse, NY 13202
cards.notes: Check the daily schedule before traveling downtown, especially because Tuesday is listed closed and Wednesday has a shorter daytime window.
cards.short_summary: A downtown food-and-music venue with midnight hours on most listed days.
cards.evidence_claim: Funk ’n Waffles lists its South Clinton Street location as open until midnight Sunday, Monday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and today.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours extend to midnight Sunday, Monday, Thursday–Saturday; Tuesday is closed and Wednesday is listed 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Oishi Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 701-5 S Crouse Ave, Syracuse, NY 13210
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online ordering option or call to verify dinner service before walking to the South Crouse Avenue address.
cards.short_summary: A Japanese and Asian restaurant that lists 11 p.m. dinner closing Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.evidence_claim: Oishi Restaurant lists its location near Syracuse University and dinner/carryout hours until 11 p.m. Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Listed dinner and carryout hours are 4–11 p.m. Tuesday–Sunday; delivery hours also extend to 11 p.m. Confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Schine Dining
cards.subtitle: Schine Student Center, Syracuse University
cards.notes: Use Campus Dining’s live hours page before heading to the student center, since the university notes that semester and summer schedules can vary.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus food hall identified by Syracuse University as open late on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says Schine Dining is in the Schine Student Center and is open late on weekends.
cards.source_title: Retail Shopping and Dining — Syracuse University
cards.access_notes: The university identifies Schine Dining as open late on weekends and directs visitors to its current Food Hall Hours page; schedules may change.

cards.title: Goldstein Food Hall
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Goldstein Student Center
cards.notes: Check Campus Dining’s live schedule before going to South Campus; this is the university’s named food-hall option in Goldstein Student Center.
cards.short_summary: A South Campus food hall that Syracuse University identifies as open late on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says Goldstein Food Hall is on the lower level of Goldstein Student Center and is open late on weekends.
cards.source_title: Retail Shopping and Dining — Syracuse University
cards.access_notes: The university identifies Goldstein Food Hall as open late on weekends and directs visitors to its current Food Hall Hours page; schedules may change.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces documented by Syracuse University for quiet work, group projects, conversation, and student events.

cards.title: Safire Room
cards.subtitle: Sixth floor, Bird Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or a laptop to the sixth floor and use the quiet-work room’s campus view for a focused session between classes.
cards.short_summary: A book-lined Bird Library room for quiet work with a panoramic campus view.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies the Safire Room on Bird Library’s sixth floor as a space for quiet work and notes its panoramic campus view.
cards.access_notes: Located in Bird Library; the library reports public access until 7 p.m. on regular business days, with extended access requiring valid SU or SUNY-ESF ID.

cards.title: Carnegie Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Carnegie Library, Shaw Quadrangle
cards.notes: Choose a table in the historic reading room when you want a dedicated quiet-study setting rather than a group lounge.
cards.short_summary: A historic, naturally lit reading room for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University describes Carnegie Library’s historic Reading Room as a quiet-study space with high ceilings, arches, and a domed skylight.
cards.access_notes: The University locates Carnegie Library on the Shaw Quadrangle and lists team rooms, workstations, and a printer room in the building.

cards.title: Noble Room
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Hendricks Chapel
cards.notes: Use the couches and chairs to compare notes with classmates; the nearby People’s Place Café is optional if you want food or coffee.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level Hendricks Chapel setting for relaxed group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University states that the Noble Room, on Hendricks Chapel’s lower level, offers couches and chairs for comparing notes with classmates.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Inside Hendricks Chapel. The chapel lists academic-year building hours of 8 a.m.–9 p.m.; confirm access around events and breaks.

cards.title: Panasci Lounge
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Schine Student Center
cards.notes: Set up at a lounge seat facing Hall of Languages when you need a quieter place to read, write, or work between activities.
cards.short_summary: A glass-filled Schine lounge with seating oriented toward Hall of Languages.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University describes Panasci Lounge as a glass-filled second-floor space in Schine Student Center facing Hall of Languages and used for assignments.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Schine Student Center; the University describes its seating as suitable for studying, group meetings, or lounging.

cards.title: The Underground
cards.subtitle: Bottom floor, Schine Student Center
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the lounge or check the campus calendar for a lecture, concert, meeting, or other scheduled event in the adjacent venue.
cards.short_summary: A Schine lower-level lounge and event venue used for campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says The Underground is on Schine Student Center’s bottom floor and that its venue is used for meetings, banquets, lectures, and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Inside Schine Student Center; event access and seating availability depend on scheduled programming.

cards.title: Mower Passage
cards.subtitle: Connecting Newhouse 1 and Newhouse 2
cards.notes: Use this indoor passage’s padded chairs and daylight for a brief reading session or a waiting spot between Newhouse classes.
cards.short_summary: A sunlit Newhouse connector with lounge seating and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies Mower Passage as the connection between Newhouse 1 and 2 and describes its padded chairs and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.access_notes: An interior connector between Newhouse 1 and Newhouse 2; access can vary with building schedules.

cards.title: Link Hall
cards.subtitle: College of Engineering and Computer Science building
cards.notes: Head to a walk-in lounge or the top-floor hallway when you need a place to read, wait, or work while looking across Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: Engineering building with walk-in lounges and a top-floor view over Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University reports that Link Hall has walk-in graduate and undergraduate lounges and a top-floor hallway overlooking Shaw Quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Most of Link Hall is used by the College of Engineering and Computer Science; use normal building access and posted policies.

cards.title: Gerry's Café
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Eggers Hall
cards.notes: Use the glass-lined seating as a daytime stop for individual work or a conversation; food is optional and service details can change.
cards.short_summary: An Eggers Hall café seating area adjacent to Maxwell Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University places Gerry’s Café on Eggers Hall’s third floor, adjacent to Maxwell Hall, and describes its glass-lined eatery and seating.
cards.access_notes: Inside Eggers Hall; the cited University story says food service was Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–3 p.m., while building access is separate.

cards.title: Hinds ICE Box
cards.subtitle: School of Information Studies
cards.notes: Bring a project team to the Innovation, Collaboration and Entrepreneurship Center for a work session or to develop an early-stage idea.
cards.short_summary: An iSchool space for project work, collaboration, and entrepreneurship.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says the Hinds ICE Box is the Innovation, Collaboration and Entrepreneurship Center for students working on projects or startup companies.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Located in the School of Information Studies; confirm availability and any reservation requirements with the school.

cards.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Library
cards.subtitle: Sims Hall
cards.notes: Work near the computer cluster or media workstation, then take time to look at the library’s rare and first-edition collections.
cards.short_summary: A Sims Hall library combining study technology with art and rare-book collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University locates the Martin Luther King Jr. Library in Sims Hall and notes its rare and first-edition collections, computer cluster, and media workstation.
cards.source_title: Ten Great Places to Study for Finals
cards.access_notes: Located in Sims Hall; check College of Arts and Sciences or building information for current access details.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented Syracuse-area places and activities where admission or participation does not require a purchase.

cards.title: Browse the university art museum
cards.subtitle: Shaffer Art Building, Syracuse University
cards.notes: Meet at the Shaffer Art Building and take time with the galleries; the museum welcomes public visitors and its exhibitions without admission.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission campus art stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Syracuse University Art Museum states that it is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; check the museum’s current exhibition information before visiting.

cards.title: See a downtown campus gallery show
cards.subtitle: Nancy Cantor Warehouse, 350 W. Fayette St.
cards.notes: Use the campus trolley or make a downtown plan around the gallery, then view the current student, faculty, or alumni exhibition together.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary exhibitions in the Nancy Cantor Warehouse.
cards.evidence_claim: The Warehouse Gallery says it is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public entry is free. The official page lists academic-year and summer hours; confirm the current exhibition schedule.

cards.title: Look through photography at Light Work
cards.subtitle: Robert B. Menschel Media Center, 316 Waverly Ave.
cards.notes: Walk over to the Menschel Media Center and view the photography and lens-based-media exhibitions during the posted gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery devoted to photography and related media.
cards.evidence_claim: Light Work states that its galleries are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free public galleries; the official page lists Monday–Thursday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with holiday closures possible.

cards.title: Catch an Urban Video Project screening
cards.subtitle: Everson Museum façade, downtown Syracuse
cards.notes: Meet downtown after dark to watch the projected moving-image exhibition on the Everson façade; bring layers and use public sidewalks.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor projected art on the Everson Museum façade.
cards.evidence_claim: Light Work says Urban Video Project presents exhibitions on the Everson Museum façade from dusk to 11 p.m., Thursday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: The program is presented outdoors from dusk to 11 p.m. Thursday–Sunday; verify the current projection schedule before going.

cards.title: Visit La Casita’s art gallery
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Building, 109 Otisco St.
cards.notes: Plan a small gallery visit at La Casita and use the exhibition as a prompt for conversation about the artists’ themes and materials.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery at Syracuse University’s La Casita.
cards.evidence_claim: La Casita states that admission to its gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free and public. Check La Casita’s current exhibition and building access details before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into Bird Library
cards.subtitle: 222 Waverly Ave., Syracuse University
cards.notes: Choose an open study area, browse periodicals, or meet quietly between classes; visitors may enter during the public-access window.
cards.short_summary: Public daytime access to Bird’s study spaces and collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Bird Library is open to the public daily until 7 p.m. on regular business days.
cards.access_notes: Public access is available until 7 p.m. on regular business days; an SU or SUNY-ESF ID is needed for extended access.

cards.entity_name: We Demand: A Legacy of Activism in America
cards.title: Explore the We Demand exhibition
cards.subtitle: Special Collections Research Center, Bird Library sixth-floor gallery
cards.notes: Visit the sixth-floor gallery to examine archival materials on activism and social reform; allow time to read the exhibition labels closely.
cards.short_summary: A free archival exhibition running through December 2026.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University Libraries says the exhibition is on view through the end of December 2026 and its public tours are free.
cards.source_title: Public Tour of We Demand: A Legacy of Activism in America
cards.access_notes: The exhibition is in Bird Library’s sixth-floor gallery through December 2026. Listed public tours are free but require registration.

cards.title: Attend a Malmgren concert
cards.subtitle: Hendricks Chapel, Syracuse University
cards.notes: Check the Hendricks Chapel calendar, then attend a scheduled Sunday concert with friends and arrive early enough to find seating.
cards.short_summary: A public concert series in Hendricks Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says the Malmgren Concert Series offers the Syracuse community arts programming at no cost.
cards.access_notes: Concert dates vary. Confirm the current Hendricks Chapel schedule before attending.

cards.title: Walk Thornden Park together
cards.subtitle: 201 Ostrom Ave., near Syracuse University
cards.notes: Use the paved walking trails, green space, lily pond, and outdoor fitness features for a low-key daytime meetup near campus.
cards.short_summary: A 76-acre city park with trails, gardens, and open space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Syracuse lists Thornden Park’s trails, green spaces, lily pond, and outdoor fitness equipment, and says city parks are open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: City parks are open daily from dawn to dusk. Do not reserve facilities; reservations carry permit fees.

cards.title: Explore the Erie Canal Museum
cards.subtitle: 1850 Syracuse Weighlock Building, downtown Syracuse
cards.notes: Take the self-guided route through the historic weighlock building, then compare the artifacts and interactive displays that catch your attention.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided canal-history museum in a historic weighlock building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Erie Canal Museum says it is open seven days a week with free admission.
cards.access_notes: The museum describes free admission; its visit page also labels contributions as pay-what-you-wish, so no purchase is required.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Syracuse University Libraries study environments, from quiet reading rooms to reservable project spaces.

cards.title: Carnegie Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Carnegie Library, second floor
cards.notes: Set up at a wooden table with a lamp and outlet, then keep calls elsewhere: this open room is designated for quiet study and is first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: A large, quiet reading room with traditional tables, lamps, and individual power access.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University Libraries describes this as a quiet, first-come, first-served reading room with wooden tables, chairs, table lamps, and outlets.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular Carnegie Library hours; quiet-area signs ask users to refrain from conversations.

cards.entity_name: Diane and Bob Miron '59 Learning Commons
cards.title: Diane and Bob Miron '59 Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor commons when you need a workstation, printer, scanner, or a table for collaborative work; seating is available first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: An open collaborative floor with public computers, printing, scanning, and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries lists public workstations, printers, scanners, tables, chairs, soft seating, and first-come, first-served access in the Miron Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: Miron Learning Commons, Bird Library 1st Floor
cards.access_notes: Located on Bird Library's first floor and available first-come, first-served during regular library access.

cards.title: Bird Library 2nd Floor
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, second floor
cards.notes: Choose a soft seat or an individual cubicle, and keep periodicals or reference materials nearby when your work benefits from a quick research break.
cards.short_summary: An airy open-study floor combining soft seating, cubicles, periodicals, and nearby reference materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University Libraries says the second floor has soft seating, individual cubicle spaces, windows, periodicals, reference materials, and regular-hours access.
cards.access_notes: Available during regular library hours.

cards.title: Bird Library 3rd through 5th Floors
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, floors three through five
cards.notes: Walk the perimeter for window-side seating, or choose soft seating, a workstation, or a table; each floor has open areas with quieter options.
cards.short_summary: Three floors of varied study seating, including window-side locations, workstations, and tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries describes open study areas on floors 3–5 with soft seating, private workstations, tables, quieter spaces, and perimeter windows.
cards.access_notes: Open areas are part of Bird Library; see library hours and floor-specific room policies for access.

cards.title: Quiet Computing Area
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, second floor
cards.notes: Bring work that needs a campus computer or scanner, then use a first-come workstation in the quiet area rather than taking calls at the desk.
cards.short_summary: A quiet computer lab with 20 workstations plus printing, scanning, and copying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries identifies this as a first-come, first-served quiet area on Bird Library's second floor with 20 workstations and scan/copy-capable printers.
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served; posted quiet-area guidance asks users to refrain from cell-phone and other conversations.

cards.title: Map Room
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, third floor beside the Service Desk
cards.notes: Spread an atlas, sheet map, or notes across one of the room's worktables; ask at the nearby Service Desk if you need help locating materials.
cards.short_summary: A study area within the map collections, furnished with large and small worktables.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries says the third-floor Map Room is a collections resource area with three large and two small worktables and cartographic materials.
cards.access_notes: Located next to the Service Desk on Bird Library's third floor; access is subject to regular library operations.

cards.title: Safire Room
cards.subtitle: Bird Library Room 605, sixth floor
cards.notes: Use the book-lined room for quiet work when the sixth floor is open, and plan to leave the camera away because photography and filming are prohibited.
cards.short_summary: A quiet sixth-floor room with book-lined walls and a campus-facing view.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries describes the Safire Room as a book-lined, quiet study space with a campus view, first-come access, and no photography or filming.
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served when Bird Library's sixth floor is open; it is not reservable.

cards.title: Plastics Pioneers Reading Room Gallery
cards.subtitle: Bird Library Room 610, sixth floor
cards.notes: Work quietly among Special Collections displays when the sixth floor is open; the room pairs a small study setting with materials from the Plastics Collection.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study room that also displays materials from Special Collections' Plastics Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries identifies Room 610 as a quiet study room on Bird Library's sixth floor that features materials from the Special Collections Plastics Collection.
cards.access_notes: Available when the sixth floor is open; quiet-area guidance asks users to refrain from conversations.

cards.entity_name: Sensory Friendly, Reservable, Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Sensory Friendly, Reservable, Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Bird Library, third and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve an individual room when you want controllable lighting and sensory tools, or request one of the two first-come rooms at the first-floor Check Out desk.
cards.short_summary: Individual academic rooms equipped with dimmable lighting, sensory discs, and fidget items.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries says eight sensory-friendly individual rooms are reservable and two are first-come, with dimmable lighting, sensory discs, and fidget items.
cards.source_title: Sensory Friendly, Reservable, Individual Study Rooms, Bird Library
cards.access_notes: For current SU and ESF-affiliated students, individual academic/research work only; rooms are available during regular library hours, for up to three hours.

cards.title: Team Rooms, Bird Library
cards.subtitle: Bird Library study rooms
cards.notes: Reserve with a group of two to five for project work, presentation practice, or virtual conferencing; connect up to four laptops to the room display.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms with a large HDMI display, whiteboard, conference table, internet, and outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries says groups of 2–5 SU or SUNY-ESF students may reserve these academic rooms, which include a display for up to four laptops and a whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Current SU or SUNY-ESF students may reserve for academic/research work during regular library hours; maximum checkout is three hours per group per day.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Marshall Street and South Crouse Avenue, the Crouse-Marshall corridors beside Syracuse University.

cards.title: Chipotle Mexican Grill — customizable entrées
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 129 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Use the 129 Marshall Street location when you want a customizable burrito, bowl, taco, salad, or quesadilla near campus.
cards.short_summary: A Marshall Street stop for build-your-own Mexican-style meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Chipotle’s official location page lists 129 Marshall St. and describes customizable burritos, bowls, quesadillas, tacos, and salads.
cards.access_notes: Official listing shows daily restaurant hours; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies — cookies and ice-cream sandwiches
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 137 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Choose this Marshall Street storefront for cookies to go or an ice-cream cookie sandwich; check the current store listing before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A dessert-focused stop on Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Insomnia Cookies at 137 Marshall St.; Visit Syracuse describes cookies and ice-cream cookie sandwiches there.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the business.

cards.title: Taste of Asia — Thai and Vietnamese dishes
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 143 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Plan a Thai or Vietnamese meal at this Marshall Street restaurant; its official site offers menu, reservations, and ordering links.
cards.short_summary: A Marshall Street restaurant for Thai and Vietnamese cooking.
cards.evidence_claim: Taste of Asia’s official site identifies its location as 143 Marshall St.; Visit Syracuse describes Thai and Vietnamese dishes.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists hours; verify them before visiting.

cards.title: Bleu Monkey Café — sushi and noodle bowls
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 163 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Use this stop when you are looking for sushi, noodle bowls, or bento boxes on Marshall Street; review the current menu first.
cards.short_summary: A Japanese-focused meal option along Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Bleu Monkey Café at 163 Marshall St.; Visit Syracuse identifies sushi, noodle bowls, and bento boxes.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours and menu directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Acropolis Pizza House — pizza-house stop
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 167 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Add this named Marshall Street pizza-house destination to a food walk and confirm its current menu and hours before you go.
cards.short_summary: A documented pizza-house destination on Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Acropolis Pizza House at 167 Marshall St.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the business.

cards.title: Panda West — Chinese seafood restaurant
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 135 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Consider this 135 Marshall Street restaurant when you want a Chinese-seafood option; verify current service details directly before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A Chinese seafood restaurant on the Marshall Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Panda West Chinese Seafood Restaurant at 135 Marshall St.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Pita Pit — customizable sandwich option
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 107 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Stop at this 107 Marshall Street location for a customizable sandwich-style meal, then confirm the current menu and service hours.
cards.short_summary: A build-to-order sandwich option on Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Pita Pit at 107 Marshall St.; Visit Syracuse says its sandwich options can be customized.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Royal Indian Grill — Indian cuisine
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 147 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Use this named Marshall Street destination when you want an Indian-cuisine option near campus; check the restaurant’s current details first.
cards.short_summary: An Indian restaurant located on Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Royal Indian Grill at 147 Marshall St.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the restaurant.

cards.title: Unique Tea House — tea-house stop
cards.subtitle: Marshall Street corridor • 171 Marshall St.
cards.notes: Make this 171 Marshall Street tea-house destination part of a daytime corridor walk, and consult the business for current offerings and hours.
cards.short_summary: A tea-house destination along Marshall Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University lists Unique Tea House at 171 Marshall St.
cards.source_title: Syracuse University Belonging and Student Success Resources
cards.access_notes: Check current hours directly with the business.

cards.title: Varsity Pizza — breakfast, wraps, and pizza
cards.subtitle: South Crouse Avenue corridor • 802 S. Crouse Ave.
cards.notes: Visit this South Crouse Avenue restaurant for breakfast, wraps, or pizza; the official site provides a gallery, menu sections, and location details.
cards.short_summary: A South Crouse Avenue restaurant with several meal formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Varsity Pizza’s official site lists 802 S. Crouse Avenue and identifies breakfast, wraps, and pizza offerings.
cards.access_notes: The official site posts weekly hours; verify them before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Syracuse traditions, from Dome game-day rituals to campus good-luck customs.

cards.title: Spot Otto the Orange
cards.subtitle: University mascot tradition
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for Otto at campus events and games; the mascot has been Syracuse’s official mascot since 1995.
cards.short_summary: Syracuse’s orange-shaped mascot is a long-running rallying symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University says Otto was officially named its mascot in 1995 and appears at games and campus events.
cards.access_notes: Look for mascot appearances at publicly scheduled University events.

cards.title: Do the Dome Stomp
cards.subtitle: JMA Wireless Dome entry ritual
cards.notes: Before entering a game at the JMA Wireless Dome, stand between the concrete pillars and join the stomp.
cards.short_summary: A pre-entry stomp turns the Dome’s pillars into part of the crowd noise.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies standing between the concrete pillars to do the Dome Stomp before entry as a Syracuse tradition.
cards.access_notes: Use only when attending a scheduled JMA Wireless Dome event; venue entry requirements apply.

cards.title: Shake Your Keys on Third Down
cards.subtitle: Syracuse football crowd ritual
cards.notes: At Syracuse football games, follow the crowd’s third-down key shake to make noise for the Orange defense.
cards.short_summary: Fans turn keys into a noisemaker when opponents face third down.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that Syracuse fans shake their keys to foil football opponents on third down.
cards.access_notes: Participate during a scheduled football game while following event staff directions.

cards.title: Stay Up Until the First Point
cards.subtitle: Syracuse basketball tipoff ritual
cards.notes: At basketball tipoff, stand and clap with the crowd until Syracuse scores its first point of the game.
cards.short_summary: The opening possession comes with a shared standing clap.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes a basketball custom of standing and clapping until the Orange score their first point.
cards.access_notes: Participate during a scheduled basketball game and remain mindful of accessible seating areas.

cards.title: Notice the Number 44
cards.subtitle: Orange football legacy tradition
cards.notes: Look for 44 around campus and at games, then visit Plaza 44 to connect the number with its honored players.
cards.short_summary: A jersey number became a recurring symbol of Syracuse football history.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls No. 44 iconic because of Jim Brown, Ernie Davis and Floyd Little, and notes its presence in Plaza 44 and campus life.
cards.access_notes: Plaza 44 is an outdoor campus landmark; observe any posted access guidance.

cards.title: Listen for the Crouse Chimes
cards.subtitle: Crouse Tower music tradition
cards.notes: Pause when the bells carry across the Hill; Chimesmasters play the alma mater, fight song and other tunes.
cards.short_summary: Student Chimesmasters make Crouse Tower a changing campus soundtrack.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Crouse Chimes began with bells installed in 1889 and that Chimesmasters continue the tradition.
cards.access_notes: Listen from public outdoor areas; tower access is not part of this activity.

cards.title: Meet the Goon Squad at Move-In
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week move-in tradition
cards.notes: During move-in, watch for the Goon Squad’s cheers and volunteer help as new students settle into residence halls.
cards.short_summary: An 80-year welcoming committee helps new students begin campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies the Goon Squad as its official welcoming committee and says it has helped new students on move-in day since 1944.
cards.source_title: Goon Squad Traditions Make Lasting Impact
cards.access_notes: This tradition occurs during University move-in programming; follow residence-hall check-in instructions.

cards.title: Mark National Orange Day
cards.subtitle: March 24 founding-anniversary tradition
cards.notes: Wear orange or join a listed service activity on March 24, Syracuse University’s annual founding-anniversary celebration.
cards.short_summary: The University’s anniversary is observed with orange gear, service and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says National Orange Day is held March 24, its 1870 founding anniversary, with orange gear, service activities and events.
cards.access_notes: Check the University events calendar for that year’s public National Orange Day activities.

cards.title: Find the Kissing Bench
cards.subtitle: Between Hall of Languages and Tolley Humanities Building
cards.notes: Visit the Class of 1912 stone bench and learn the campus saying that couples who sit together are destined to wed.
cards.short_summary: A stone bench carries a playful Syracuse relationship legend.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes the Kissing Bench as a Class of 1912 gift and records the tradition that couples who sit there are destined to wed.
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors on the west side of Hall of Languages; respect other visitors’ space.

cards.title: Rub the Dog’s Paw for Luck
cards.subtitle: Carnegie Library exam ritual
cards.notes: Before an exam or important moment, visit Diana the Huntress at Carnegie Library and offer a good wish while rubbing the dog’s paw.
cards.short_summary: Students pair an art landmark with a small pre-exam good-luck ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says tradition holds that rubbing the dog’s paw on Diana the Huntress while offering a good wish invites exam success.
cards.access_notes: The statue is at Carnegie Library; use public building access and avoid obstructing others.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Syracuse University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through campus landmarks, useful student spaces, and a current event-finding tool.

cards.title: Start with a campus wayfinding pass
cards.subtitle: Main Campus
cards.notes: Open the interactive map before heading out, then use it to identify classrooms, dining options, and the next stop on your walk.
cards.short_summary: Use Syracuse’s official map to get oriented on Main Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University’s interactive campus map can be used to search campus, find classrooms and dining options, and wayfind.
cards.access_notes: Use the online interactive map before or during the walk.

cards.title: See the building where campus began
cards.subtitle: 101 Crouse Dr.
cards.notes: Pause outside the Hall of Languages and use its historic setting to anchor your first walk through the academic core of campus.
cards.short_summary: Visit Syracuse University’s first campus building.
cards.evidence_claim: Built between 1871 and 1873, the Hall of Languages was Syracuse University’s first building and still serves as the home of Arts and Sciences.
cards.access_notes: A campus landmark; enter only during applicable building hours.

cards.title: Find the relocated observatory
cards.subtitle: Main Campus
cards.notes: Continue to Holden Observatory and look for the historic structure that now houses an astronomy learning center and working telescope.
cards.short_summary: Add a historic observatory to the campus loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Holden Observatory houses the Patricia Meyers Druger Astronomy Learning Center and a working telescope manufactured in 1895.
cards.access_notes: View the building exterior; check the learning center for any public programming.

cards.title: Walk the Old Row
cards.subtitle: Main Campus
cards.notes: Keep the route moving along Old Row, where Crouse College is part of the University’s early line of historic campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: Trace one of the historic buildings on Syracuse’s Old Row.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies Crouse College, built in 1889, as part of Old Row.
cards.source_title: Buildings That Make Syracuse University | Syracuse University
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; building access may vary.

cards.title: Continue past Tolley
cards.subtitle: Main Campus
cards.notes: Add Tolley Building to the same historic stretch, then compare its place in Old Row with the buildings you have already passed.
cards.short_summary: Continue the architecture-focused campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Syracuse University identifies the Tolley Building, built in 1888, as part of Old Row.
cards.source_title: Buildings That Make Syracuse University | Syracuse University
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; building access may vary.

cards.title: Get a feel for Bird Library
cards.subtitle: 222 Waverly Ave.
cards.notes: Stop in during public hours to locate open study areas, the Quiet Reading Room, and the first-floor learning commons for later use.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself to Syracuse’s main library and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Bird Library has seven floors with open study areas, a Quiet Reading Room, the Learning Commons, and research and printing services.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily until 7 p.m. on regular business days; extended access requires valid SU or SUNY-ESF ID.

cards.entity_name: Hildegarde and J. Myer Schine Student Center
cards.title: Use Schine as a meet-up point
cards.subtitle: 200 Waverly Ave.
cards.notes: Meet up in Schine, then note the dining center, lounges, event spaces, campus store, and student services located in the building.
cards.short_summary: Make the student center a practical gathering stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Schine Student Center houses dining, a campus store, event spaces, meeting rooms, lounges, and offices.
cards.access_notes: Building services and dining availability vary; check the student center’s current information before visiting.

cards.title: Take a quiet chapel stop
cards.subtitle: 121 Crouse Drive
cards.notes: Step into Hendricks Chapel for a quieter campus pause, and check its programming if you want to return for a concert or gathering.
cards.short_summary: Pause at a campus center for spiritual, ethical, and cultural life.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendricks Chapel serves as a center for religious, spiritual, moral, and ethical life and hosts student religious and spiritual groups.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are 8 a.m.–9 p.m.; the building has an accessible side entrance and elevator.

cards.title: Locate the Dome before game day
cards.subtitle: 900 Irving Ave.
cards.notes: Walk by the JMA Wireless Dome so you know the approach, then check the official schedule and ticket details before attending an event.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to Syracuse’s main athletics and event venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The JMA Wireless Dome is Syracuse University Athletics’ venue at 900 Irving Avenue, with guest services available for events.
cards.source_title: JMA Wireless Dome Contact Info | Syracuse University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Public entry is event-specific; athletics states gates open according to the event schedule.

cards.title: Choose one approved campus event
cards.subtitle: Syracuse University online community
cards.notes: Log in with your NetID, filter upcoming events or organizations by interest, and RSVP only for an option that fits your own schedule.
cards.short_summary: Use Syracuse’s student portal to find an event or organization.
cards.evidence_claim: ’Cuse Activities lets Syracuse University students browse events, connect with recognized student organizations, and RSVP to Student Engagement events.
cards.access_notes: Available to Syracuse University and SUNY-ESF students, faculty, and staff using an SU NetID; individual event requirements vary.
